checks.label: Most recent Form 990
checks.detail: This is the period of the most recent return the IRS has processed, at month precision, taken from the Business Master File. It is not a filing date: processing lags filing by weeks to more than a year, so the actual return may be considerably more recent.

checks.label: Years since filing
checks.detail: Roughly 1 year(s) since the end of the most recent tax period the IRS has processed. This comes from the Business Master File, which records a processing period rather than a filing date and can lag actual filing by more than a year, so treat it as approximate. Automatic revocation triggers after three consecutive years without filing a Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-N. Confirm against the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search before acting on it.

checks.detail: The IRS records this organization under NTEE code W20. NTEE codes are self-reported at application and are frequently out of date, so it is worth confirming it still describes the work.

checks.label: Single audit
checks.detail: Your current fiscal year began 2026-01-01, so the threshold that applies to it is $1,000,000 in federal awards expended. It rose from $750,000 for years beginning before 2024-10-01. This tool cannot tell you how much you expended — that figure is not in the public datasets it publishes. Count everything federal, including subawards passed through a state agency, a university, or a larger nonprofit, and count what was spent rather than what was received. Your Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards is where that number lives.
